As a part of the current issue we were expecting:
1. Implement chainlink oracles for collateral token prices
2. Check that our current [Dollar oracle](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibTWAPOracle.sol) works as expected (and can't be easily manipulated, but it depends on the curve metapool liquidity, as far as I understand)
@gitcoindev You could delegate some of the tasks to me (collateral price via chainlink feature or fixing Dollar curve price). We must have this issue done till 31 December.
@pavlovcik Permit was not generated, not sure if this is expected. As far as I understand we owe 300 USD to @gitcoindev

@pavlovcik 
I've just successfully decrypted this private key for the `0xf87ca4583c792212e52720d127e7e0a38b818ad1` address. I will DM you `x25519_private_key` and `x25519_public_key` for you to double check.
Yes
This is public key, not private, so it is safe to share it. Naming could've been better.
Yes. The only risk is that if `X25519_PRIVATE_KEY` is leaked (on our side) then a malicious actor will be able to decrypt partners' private keys (if there are in public repos, not private).
No. Partners encrypt with `X25519_PUBLIC_KEY` (which is available in [public](https://github.com/pavlovcik/pay.ubq.fi/blob/b259f9736212ca40dac241eb40b2b961bb3d6f39/static/scripts/onboarding/onboarding.ts#L32)) while for decrypting `X25519_PRIVATE_KEY` is necessary which is stored only on the bot's side (i.e. backend).
 > Are there any improvements you can suggest?
 You've already proposed that we need critical env variables rotation mechanism and `X25519_PRIVATE_KEY` is the 1st candidate for such rotation.
We'll gradually move to smth like "take the median price from chainlink, curve, uniswap, other oracle provider". Right now chainlink is the fastest to implement, safest and most reliable solution.

We have the [UbiquityPoolFacet](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/7a70182d49a0b9dc947c9925a5d28edc49c28b0d/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/UbiquityPoolFacet.sol) contract (which uses [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/7a70182d49a0b9dc947c9925a5d28edc49c28b0d/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) library under the hood) which is responsible for minting/redeeming Dollar tokens for collateral.
Example:
1. User calls [mintDollar()](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/7a70182d49a0b9dc947c9925a5d28edc49c28b0d/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/UbiquityPoolFacet.sol#L20) and sends 100 LUSD as collateral
2. User gets 100 Dollars
Now check this [test](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/blob/5b6bcd03837b2f8cc704593534e9742f6cc5af75/packages/contracts/test/diamond/facets/UbiquityPoolFacet.t.sol#L345). It basically simulates the [calcMintDollarAmount()](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/7a70182d49a0b9dc947c9925a5d28edc49c28b0d/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L382) method responsible for calculating how much Dollars should be minted/redeemed in exchange for collateral tokens.
The calculation seems to be wrong because when we try to get the collateral price in USD here https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/7a70182d49a0b9dc947c9925a5d28edc49c28b0d/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L438 we use cumulative price which seems to be wrong. As a result user gets much more Dollars in exchange for collateral. Example:
1. User calls [mintDollar()](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/7a70182d49a0b9dc947c9925a5d28edc49c28b0d/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/UbiquityPoolFacet.sol#L20) and sends 100 LUSD as collateral
2. User gets `~239561778028138198.47` Dollars which is way too high
As a part of the current issue we should add a new method to the [oracle faucet](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/7a70182d49a0b9dc947c9925a5d28edc49c28b0d/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/TWAPOracleDollar3poolFacet.sol) which will be responsible for fetching collateral token prices in USD.
Possible options:
1. Curve TWAP (we already use it for the Dollar token)
2. Chainlink oracles

We could remove the `onlyAdmin` modifier because, as far as I understand, there is no issue if somebody else would fetch the latest collateral price.
Another point is that collateral prices should be updated automatically before any collateral price related operations. I couldn't find this feature in the https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/dac1794b832a8883fa15794eb5afa7f4054680a8/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol
It makes sense to install https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink as a dependency instead of copy-pasting the code.

Source https://github.com/ubiquibot/comment-incentives/actions/runs/7316071529/job/19930337990#step:5:631
### Context
- The bot can directly read the invoking organization's UbiquiBot Config (both the org's and repo's)
- You can see in the logs that the bot reads `evmPrivateEncrypted: 'OwWrEtDWl7mq79FM-mb4hbrU9uBtffvX3MPuEjcXenWocH-JS4SVYXFr0rm-wYuWHnwrzLYvatKGywShwMVCEZw6f-g2XyDIPdrEzAHCZ8WH_v76kJsVEOGEe8qRvy4z6ai0YGFpzV4iFB8NfZEg5kb9k88',` just fine. 
- I understand that the decryption failed due to a mismatched `X25519_PRIVATE_KEY`?
### Questions
- In order to just make this work, perhaps you can help me regenerate the proper `X25519_PRIVATE_KEY` so that we can continue to use the existing `evmPrivateEncrypted`? Or you can help me set up a new key pair that will work?
   - I just checked the [source code](https://github.com/pavlovcik/pay.ubq.fi/blob/b259f9736212ca40dac241eb40b2b961bb3d6f39/static/scripts/onboarding/onboarding.ts#L32) (we obviously need a more secure replacement for this onboarding UI.) and used the identical `X25519_PRIVATE_KEY` but the run [still failed](https://github.com/ubiquibot/comment-incentives/actions/runs/7316183062/job/19930563324#step:5:665). 
- Is this approach okay, where the bot can read the `evmPrivateEncrypted` of every partner, and we simply store a single `X25519_PRIVATE_KEY` in the bot secrets?
- If any partner can encrypt their EVM private key, doesn't that mean they necessarily have access to our source `X25519_PRIVATE_KEY`?
- Are there any improvements you can suggest?
### Remarks
Something seems off: 
1. I regenerated a new pair and [updated the encrypted private key](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-config/commit/568440dea0155a7e9fc839d6e8436aabb71ac1e3). 
2. It [sort of ran once](https://github.com/ubiquibot/comment-incentives/actions/runs/7316295068/job/19930779580#step:5:730) right after that fix.
3. I updated the `X25519_PRIVATE_KEY` in the ubiquibot org (the one hosting the comment incentives plugin) to the correct value, and now I'm having the same key related issues.
Given all these new insights, I'm starting to think that the only way forward is for plugins to request a transaction on partner gnosis safes. If anybody can make a plugin and freely maintain/update them, then it seems a bit risky for them to have access to the shared X25519 key which allows them to access any private keys encrypted with the same X25519 key.
I'm not sure. To be honest I never felt mastery around the X25519 key related feature so it's possible that I'm making a mistake in the configuration.

Indeed a well thought chainlink it's a heavily centrilized organization which the only good thing they provide it's infrastructure as a service and well known set of poketing of smart contracts, and use cases in with heavily demanded protocols that are using it, but that's it
the implementation looks good and the revamped tests are much better now, once again everyone good work here

the testing should be mocked, and not really interfacing with mainnet, this was deprecated a while ago, with #682 (where there is an open issue, to work on something that can do mainnet tests too)  If I recall, that's why all tests do not fork any mainnet, but in your testing you can use --fork-url to test stuff to mainnet on your enviroment

Yes, however you'll be only be able to accomplish this by running `forge` on top of the contracts folder and not on top of the `ubiquity-dollar` repo like doing it with the yarn namespace, instead you would directly using `forge` on `/contracts`
version naming on import path? doesn't look approachable, could you achieve it in a different way?

why we should cast the value to uint80?
yeah i see now this is part of the implementation
it's what a good programmer does
